title: Screen reader is not announcing the visual label on the 'Fullscreen' button in windows
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary Screen reader is not announcing the visual label on the 'Fullscreen' button in windows. Screen reader users will be impacted as the visual label of the “Fullscreen” button is not announced. comments.body:
**To help Streamlit prioritize this feature, react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your vote helps us identify which enhancements matter most to our users.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16148)

Testing the new reproducing issues skill ([not merged yet](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16054)):

### Triage: confirmed 🐛
Thanks for the detailed report and the workaround script — reproduced and root-caused.
**Live repro:** https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-16148
**Full investigation notes:** https://issues.streamlit.app/agent_wiki_explorer?file=pull-requests/16054/gh-16148-notes.md
#### What's happening
Every fullscreen-capable element (images, charts, dataframes, etc.) renders a **Fullscreen** button with a fixed accessible name `aria-label="Fullscreen"`. It never references the element it belongs to, so on a page with several images/charts a screen reader announces a list of identical "Fullscreen button" controls with no way to tell them apart.
Confirmed on **1.57.0** with two captioned images — both buttons expose the same accessible name:

| Image caption | Fullscreen button `aria-label` |
| --- | --- |
| Federal Command Center | `Fullscreen` |
| DoD Network Architecture | `Fullscreen` |
This is a longstanding behavior (the label is a frontend constant), so it's **not a regression** — it's present on `develop` too.
#### Root cause
The toolbar hard-codes the fullscreen action's label, which becomes the button's `aria-label`, and no element caption/title is plumbed through:
- `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/Toolbar/Toolbar.tsx` — `<ToolbarAction label="Fullscreen" … />` and `aria-label={label}`
- Callers like `ImageList.tsx` already have the caption in scope but don't pass it to `<Toolbar>`.
#### Likely fix
Thread an optional accessible label through `Toolbar`/`ToolbarAction` and set it to something like `"Fullscreen: {caption}"` when a caption/title is available (keeping the visible tooltip short), falling back to plain "Fullscreen" otherwise. Small–Medium change; good candidate for an outside contribution.
#### Workaround for app authors
The client-side script from the report works — patch each button's `aria-label` to include its caption. See the "Workaround" section of the [live repro](https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-16148).
**Priority: P3** — a genuine but minor accessibility issue: not a regression, a workaround exists, and only screen-reader users are affected (the button *is* labelled, just not uniquely). 👍 on the issue if this is impacting you — enough signal can bump the priority.
